title: About API Clients and AI Agents

blocks.text: You can access Zscaler API resources using API clients or AI agents. You can configure and manage API clients and AI agents in the Zscaler Admin Console, along with their authentication information and necessary scope to access the API resources. Authentication Service includes an OAuth 2.1 authorization server that validates authorization requests by API clients and AI Agents. It issues access tokens that authorize clients accessing the API resources via the OneAPI server.

Authentication Service supports the Client Credentials and Authorization Code grant types. The Client Credentials grant type enables machine-to-machine API access without user interaction, while the Authorization Code grant type is an interactive flow where users consent to authorize API clients and AI agents to act on their behalf, limiting client entitlements based on user administrative permissions.
API clients and AI agents provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Access API resources across Zscaler services through a consistent API experience.
Securely access API resources through Authentication Service and role-based access control (RBAC).
Use the Client Credentials or Authorization Code grant type with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) to support machine-to-machine and user-delegated API access.
Configure AI agents, including Claude Code and ChatGPT, using Client Identity Metadata Documents (CIMD) for automated client registration.
Authorize API access through user consent and manage or revoke authorization grants.

blocks.text: If your organization uses Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), administrator roles for Authentication Service and some Zscaler services are managed on a different Role Management page. To learn more, see About Role Management. Unified RBAC is a feature in limited availability. To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.

blocks.heading: About the API Clients and AI Agents Page

blocks.text: On the API Clients and AI Agents page (Administration > API > API Clients), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Add an API client or AI agent.
Search for a client.
Export the list of clients as a CSV file.
Refresh the table data.
Add or remove columns from the table.
View the list of API clients and AI agents you've configured. For each API client or AI agent, you can see:
Name: The name of the client.
Status: The status (Active or Inactive) of the client.
Client ID: The unique identifier for the client.
Client Owner: The user assigned as owner for the client.
Client Team: The team to which the client owner belongs.
Edit or delete an API client or AI agent.
Disable the API client or AI agent, and view tokens.
Limit the number of records displayed per page. You can choose to display 10, 25, 50, or 100 entries per page.
Go to a specific page or move to the next or previous page.
